value noun and verb

worth

also worth, be worth, value highly, valuable, think highly of, value more, think more of, not care a straw, not give a damn, be valuable

classical

Plaut. Aul. 4.10.60: nūllus est tam parvī pretiī (Lewis & Short)
Liv. 39.6.9: in pretiō esse
M-O s.v. value, worth

pretium, pretiī n.

noun, second declension · Declension on Wiktionary

worth, value; price

Of great or little value, magnī, parvī pretiī; to be valued, prized, in pretiō esse (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • magnī (parvī, plūris, tantī) esse — be worth much (little, more, so much)

    phrase: genitive of value · also used · classical · Phaedr. 4.25.1–2: quae plūris esset

    To value something is to say in the genitive what it is worth: magnī aestimāre, magnī facere (Quint. 11.1.38), ūnius assis aestimāre, not to give a penny for (Catull. 5.3). With verbs of valuing the genitive is used throughout, and comedy adds floccī, naucī, “not a straw”; with verbs of buying and costing only tantī, quantī, plūris, minōris (see cost a lot).

  • aestimō, aestimāre, aestimāvī, aestimātum — to value, put a price on

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Dom. 44: domum ēmit prope dīmidiō cārius quam aestimābat (Lewis & Short) · Conjugation on Wiktionary

  • valor, valōris m. — value

    noun, third declension · also used · medieval · M-O s.v. value, worth (Marco Polo, c. 1300) · Declension on Wiktionary

    In antiquity only in a glossary (Lewis & Short); the medieval word.

  • pretium habēre — be worth something, be valuable

    also used · classical · Cato Agr. 2.7: vēndat oleum, sī pretium habeat (Lewis & Short s.v. pretium); Traupman 131, 401

Examples

  • formīca et musca contendēbant ācriter quae plūris esset

    the ant and the fly were arguing hotly which of them was worth morePhaedr. 4.25.1–2

  • rūmōrēsque senum sevēriōrum omnēs ūnius aestimēmus assis

    and let’s value all the gossip of grumpy old men at a single pennyCatull. 5.2–3

  • Dionȳsium semper equidem, ut scīs, dīlēxī, sed cotīdiē plūris faciō

    I have always been fond of Dionysius, as you know, but I value him more every dayCic. Att. 5.9.2

  • Neque ego illum maneō, neque floccī faciō

    I’m not waiting for him, and I don’t care a straw about himPlaut. Men. 423

See also price, cost a lot, expensive, cheap, interest.
